title: Decide the error reporting surface: in-session error banner with a "Tell us about it" report action
decision: Every failure surfaced to a player during a session shall be presented as a clear, plain-language error message in the session surface, accompanied by a "Tell us about it" action that lets the reporting player submit a report of the failure from within the application. The error message states what failed and what the player can do next; the report action captures the failure context and the player's account of it and routes it to the team for triage. The error surface is a single, consistent presentation used for all in-session failures (adventure import rejection, session join or control rejection, and any other failure the player encounters), rather than per-feature error treatments.
rationale: The founder decided that failures must show a clear error message with a "Tell us about it" button, on the stated reason that this is how the team gets notified of bugs and improves the product. That decision fixes both halves of the surface: the message must be clear to a non-technical player mid-session, and the report path must exist as a first-class action rather than an afterthought. A single shared error surface wins over per-feature error handling because the session is a continuous, shared experience: players are mid-turn and cannot be dropped into divergent failure flows, and a uniform surface keeps the failure visible to the whole group while still letting the affected player report it. It also keeps the reporting path identical across the many distinct failure points the SRS defines, so the team receives comparable reports instead of a scatter of ad-hoc messages.

options_considered.option: Per-feature error handling, where each failing capability (adventure import, session join, character control) defines its own message and recovery flow
options_considered.reason: Rejected because it fragments the failure experience mid-session and produces inconsistent, non-comparable reports, while the founder's decision calls for one clear message plus one reporting action.

options_considered.option: Silent or log-only failure handling, with failures recorded for the team but not shown to players
options_considered.reason: Rejected because it directly contradicts the founder's decision that players see a clear error message, and it leaves players unable to act when something fails during a session.

options_considered.option: Error message with a generic support contact (email or external help link) instead of an in-application report action
options_considered.reason: Rejected because it pushes players out of the session to report a failure and yields reports without the failure context, weakening the bug-notification purpose the founder gave as the reason for the decision.
